errors.description: Because the option is a matched pair, both welts must stay in frame, and in a 3:4 portrait frame that forces the whole waistcoat front from the neckline V to the pointed hem into shot. The two welts therefore occupy well under the 40-80% of frame area the CLOSE CROP directive targets, even though they are unmistakably the subject.
errors.expected: the pair of welts filling 40-80% of the frame
errors.actual: the pair of welts spans about three quarters of the frame width but only a narrow horizontal band of its height
errors.correction: no correction required for accuracy; a landscape frame would be the only way to raise the fill ratio without dropping one welt out of shot

lockedFeatures: orientation: waistcoat front, model facing camera - CORRECT
EXACTLY TWO welt pockets, one per side - CORRECT (counted: 2)
welts are SLANTED, not horizontal - CORRECT, measured at about 25 degrees from horizontal against the drawing's 24 degrees
slant direction mirror-symmetric about the placket, the end nearer the centre front sitting HIGHER than the outer end on both sides - CORRECT
welts are small and narrow - single narrow welt, no flap, no patch - CORRECT
welt length relative to button spacing - CORRECT (1.19 button-spacings rendered against 1.13 drawn)
welt distance from the centre placket - CORRECT (0.81 button-spacings rendered against 0.87 drawn)
welt height on the waistcoat, sitting at the third-button level - CORRECT
FIVE buttons down the placket with worked buttonholes - CORRECT, matches the five buttons drawn
no lower pockets and no other pocket of any kind, exactly as the drawing shows - CORRECT
two pressed vertical front seams/darts flanking the placket at about 1.4 button-spacings from centre - CORRECT, matches the drawn dart lines
V neckline and pointed hem - CORRECT
fine navy wool suiting, both welts in the same navy cloth as the body - CORRECT
zero text, numbers, arrows, leader lines, red guide marks or callouts - CORRECT; the red welt outlines in the drawing were read as highlights and rendered as navy cloth, never in red
notes: Attempt 1. Checked one element at a time against the drawing and measured proportionally using button spacing as the ruler, so the comparison does not depend on absolute scale: welt count 2, slant angle 25 vs 24 degrees, welt length 1.19 vs 1.13 button-spacings, distance from placket 0.81 vs 0.87 button-spacings, welt height at the third button in both, five buttons in both, dart positions 1.4 vs 1.39 button-spacings. Slant direction is mirror-symmetric with the centre-front end high, as drawn. No lower pockets were invented, no flap was added, no red was traced from the highlight marks, and the frame carries no annotation. The only finding is the framing note above, which is forced by the option being a symmetric pair in a portrait frame.
